title.value: The generalizability of pre-processing techniques on the accuracy and fairness of data-driven building models: A case study
title.justification: The title has been extracted directly from the provided text of the article.
title.quote: The generalizability of pre-processing techniques on the accuracy and fairness of data-driven building models: A case study

extractions.description: The paper investigates the performance of different pre-processing techniques to enhance the accuracy and fairness of data-driven building models (DDBMs). These models utilize building-related data to predict variables like indoor temperature and energy consumption. The study introduces a new sequentially balanced sampling (SBS) method and compares it with existing techniques to balance training datasets, addressing accuracy and fairness issues induced by varied data conditions. The results offer guidance on selecting pre-processing techniques to optimize predictive performance under diverse data distributions.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper focuses on improving building energy consumption predictions and modeling, which ties directly into energy efficiency in buildings, a key area for climate change mitigation.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: In recent years, massive data collected from buildings made development and application of data-driven building models is a hot research topic.

primary_category.justification: The study's focus on improving data-driven models for building energy consumption aligns with Climate Change Mitigation goals, specifically under Energy Efficiency in Buildings.
primary_category.quote: These data could be used as a basis to develop data-driven building models (DDBMs) to predict indoor air temperature, energy consumption, thermal comfort, occupancy status/numbers, indoor air quality, fire hazard, or HVAC system performance.

secondary_categories.justification: The focus of the paper is specifically on data-driven models for energy efficiency in buildings without substantial crossover into other predefined categories.
secondary_categories.quote: In this study, a sequentially balanced sampling (SBS) technique is proposed.

applications.value: Lighting status prediction for building energy efficiency
applications.justification: The paper presents a case study focused on predicting lighting status as part of building energy management.
applications.quote: Totally, 4960 cases are carried out to apply these pre-processing techniques to process training dataset before developing 4 types of classifiers for one-week ahead lighting status prediction of 155 lights in 16 apartments through a year.
